note: The check suite runs ONLY checks registered here (founding spec §4).
Registration requires an admission record: the named defect the check
caught or the contract it uniquely carries, the licensing issue, and a
removal signal declared at birth. An unregistered check file is dead
code; one meta check asserts the registry and the checks/ tree agree.
Every removal signal names its observing instrument (kogaki#113):
removal_instrument is `act: <the act that already happens and owes the
removal row>`, `none: <why no act in this repository can observe it>`,
or `probe: <tree-local shell predicate>` (exit 0 = the signal's
condition now holds; exit 1 = not yet; anything else = the probe could
not establish). Probes are evaluated by check-registry-conformance.sh,
which renders candidates report-only — removal stays a judgment.
Every admission record carries RE-EXECUTABLE EFFICACY EVIDENCE
(kogaki#243). The named defect above is a claim about what this check
CATCHES, and registration used to take it on the author's word —
constrain-generation applied to check EXISTENCE, never to check
EFFICACY. `efficacy` names the counterfactual instead: the case that
CONSTRUCTS the named defect and asserts the check REFUSES it.
`case: <path>::<verbatim label>` — the payload is the path, `::`,
and the label, WITH NOTHING APPENDED; human prose goes in the
sibling `efficacy_note`, on the convention `runtime_ms_note` sets.
`none: <why no counterfactual exists in this tree>` — the honest
state, and it is a MEASUREMENT rather than a deferral marker.
check-registry-conformance.sh refuses a `case:` unless <path> exists
and contains <label> literally and EXACTLY ONCE. What that buys,
claimed precisely because overstating it would be the very defect
kogaki#243 names: editing or deleting the cited text breaks the entry
that cites it, and a label too generic to identify one case is
refused as non-unique. What it does NOT decide: that the cited text
is a COMPLETE case label rather than part of one, or that it occurs
in code rather than in a comment. Both are judgments about meaning,
and a language-aware parser for them would be a lint over judgment.
Shape and resolution are gated; whether the counterfactual is a GOOD
one is judgment and is never gated — the split `probe:` runs under.
A member that DELEGATES its assertions to another artifact's fixture
pass carries `case_floor` (kogaki#661). Such a member can verify that
the pass RAN CLEAN and cannot, by the same evidence, verify that the
pass STILL ASSERTS ANYTHING: an exit code and an output token both
IMPROVE as the cases disappear, so both survive the deletion of every
one. Measured at kogaki#659 — a pass reporting `0 case(s) pass` exits 0
and prints its own token. `case_floor` is the minimum count the pass
must report. THE COMPARISON RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (kogaki#970): below
the floor the member FAILS because cases were LOST, and ABOVE it the
member FAILS because cases were ADDED and the floor was not advanced in
the same act.
THE ORIGINAL GROUND FOR A FLOOR RATHER THAN AN EXACT COUNT IS AMENDED
HERE RATHER THAN SILENTLY CONTRADICTED. It read: `a floor rather than an
exact count, because asserting the exact number turns every legitimate
new case into a failing check, which is the pressure that gets the
assertion deleted.` That was a real objection and it was about FRICTION,
so it is answered at the friction rather than dismissed: the upward
refusal names the exact one-line registry edit that discharges it, so a
sitting that adds a case is told what to do in the same breath as being
stopped, and the edit lands in the commit that added the case.
WHAT THE ONE-SIDED FLOOR COST, measured rather than argued (kogaki#970):
`terrain-runtime` declared 83 against a pass reporting 96. `N < FLOOR` is
green for every N above the floor, so the 13-case gap was undetectable —
any case inside it could have been deleted and the member would still
have passed. Six of the eight members declaring a floor sat exactly at
it and two had drifted, and nothing in the suite could tell those two
states apart. A ratchet advanced by hand at some increments and not
others is a ratchet that stops holding.
THE DECREMENT GATE BELOW IS UNTOUCHED, and mechanizing the increment
ratifies no new authority: the owner ruling of 2026-08-26 already made an
increment free, so what changed is that a free act is now also a
REQUIRED one. The rule is carried by check-registry-conformance.sh's
`validate_floor_exceeds_arm`, which is stated over the DECLARATION rather
than the delegating class — a member declaring a floor owes both arms —
so member N+1 is covered by the rule and not by a list somebody
remembered to extend.
It is REQUIRED of any registered check whose file spawns another
artifact's self-test, and that class is DETECTED rather than
enumerated: the dispatch shape is what conformance matches, so member
N+1 is covered by the match and not by a list somebody remembered to
extend.
LOWERING `case_floor` IS AN ADMISSION-CLASS CHANGE (owner ruling
2026-08-26). Without this the field is the silent-shrinkage channel one
hop removed: deleting a case goes red while decrementing the floor
beside it goes green. So a decrement owes a paired `case_floor_note`
naming the case(s) retired, and check-registry-conformance.sh DENIES an
unpaired decrement — deny rather than report, at the same strictness an
incomplete admission record already draws, because the ruling's own
terms are that a decrement needs the same review path as admitting a
member. The comparison reads the floor at the base commit, resolved on
the idiom check-consult-receipts.sh already uses; where no base
resolves, the row renders CANNOT-DETERMINE and never a pass — an
absent input owes could-not-establish rather than the healthy-looking
answer an absent-reads-as-unchanged coercion produces (kogaki#116).
An INCREMENT is free and owes nothing: adding cases is the direction
the floor exists to protect.
WHERE THE COUNT IS READ FROM is fixed here, because four members cite this
note for it (kogaki#661, AC10). The contract on the PASS is that it emits a
NON-NEGATIVE INTEGER count its own member can locate; the EXTRACTION is the
MEMBER'S OWN, declared in that member's file. Deliberately not one grammar
imposed on every runtime: the delegating passes print their counts three
different ways today — `terrain self-test: 18 case(s) pass`, `cite-check
self-test: 15 case(s) pass` and `fixture pass: 10/10 owner-register cases`
— and unifying them would make a decision about check plumbing get paid for
by edits to three unrelated runtimes. A member that cannot locate a count in
its pass's output FAILS: an unreadable floor is not a pass, on the same
ground as a base that will not resolve.
STILL OPEN, named rather than left: a member whose pass prints no parseable
figure at all. All four print one today; deciding what such a member owes is
its own act (deferred slot `delegating-member-with-no-parseable-count`).
OPTIONAL PER-ENTRY KEY `serial: true` (kogaki#789). The suite runs its
members CONCURRENTLY and prints the log in registry order; an entry that
cannot share the working tree with another member declares `serial: true`
and is run alone, before the pool. NO MEMBER DECLARES IT TODAY, and the
absence is a reading rather than an oversight: `runs-retention` and
`registry-conformance` are the only members touching shared paths and both
only READ them. `CHECKS_JOBS=1` in the environment restores fully serial
execution for a whole run. Neither switch changes what any member checks or
what the log says — the runner's own header carries the argument.

admission.contract:
registry/tree agreement, both ways (an unregistered check file is dead code, a registered file that does not exist is a dangling entry), plus admission-shape validation: every registered entry carries a non-empty admission record — the contracts this file's own note declares and nothing else carries.

PLUS the DELEGATING-MEMBER FLOOR (kogaki#661, story 1.92): a member whose file spawns another artifact's fixture pass owes `case_floor`, and the class is DETECTED by dispatch shape rather than enumerated, so member N+1 is covered by the match. The floor's own edit is gated in one direction only — a DECREMENT owes a paired `case_floor_note` and is DENIED without one, at the strictness an incomplete admission record draws, because lowering a floor is an admission-class change (owner ruling 2026-08-26); an INCREMENT owes nothing. An unresolvable base renders CANNOT-DETERMINE and never a pass. Declared limit, carried in the check's own words beside the pattern: the match is over TEXT, so a file merely CONTAINING the dispatch shape is indistinguishable from one that runs it — the same boundary `efficacy` declares between code and comment, and the same refusal of a language-aware parser as a lint over judgment.

PLUS the REGISTERING-MEMBER DESCRIBED-CASE RULE (kogaki#990): a member that registers its cases by id owes a `contract` that describes each one, and the class is DETECTED by the registration call rather than enumerated, so member N+1 is covered by the match exactly as it is for the delegating class above. An id is described by `(<id>)` or by `(<stem>)`, its leading run of letters, and BOTH spellings are admitted because the two vocabularies differ by design — a registration id disambiguates where a reused letter cannot, while `contract` speaks in letters; requiring the LITERAL id fired on 13 of one member's 35 ids at the head this entered on, every one of them described, which is a false red on the naming convention rather than on an omission. A member registering no cases is outside the class, and an EMPTY contract is left to the incomplete-record failure above rather than double-reported here. Declared limit, carried beside the pattern in the check's own words: this file is inside the set its own pattern searches, so the registration call is named in prose WITHOUT its argument parentheses — the rule's first run reported THIS member as registering a case it does not have. What it does not prove, stated rather than implied: that a clause says the RIGHT thing about its case. A mention is mechanically checkable and adequacy is not, so the rule refuses the SILENCE and never grades the prose — and it inherits the registering member's own blind side, since a case with no registration site is invisible to both. THE PATTERN READS ALL THREE QUOTED SPELLINGS of the registration call and names the fourth shape as a THIRD declared limit: a call taking a variable registers an id that is not in the text, so no reader of the text can recover it (PR #1000 round 1).

MUTATION EVIDENCE for the kogaki#661 floor branches (assert-by-breaking-once, run 2026-08-26 end to end against a base carrying floors, each applied once and restored): dropping `case_floor` from a delegating member FAILED by name; a floor of 0 FAILED as malformed, and the same for a negative, a string, a bool and a float; an unpaired decrement 18 -> 5 FAILED naming both numbers; THE SAME decrement paired with a `case_floor_note` was ACCEPTED, which is the case that stops the deny passing vacuously by refusing everything; an INCREMENT rendered 0 decrements and owed nothing; and an unresolvable base rendered CANNOT-DETERMINE rather than the healthy-looking pass. The class detector's own limit is exercised too: a file carrying the words `self-test` in a comment and in a failure label, WITHOUT the dispatch, is not in the class — the case that keeps the pattern from reaching check-anchor-resolve.sh. Recorded rather than asserted because this member's whole subject is admission records whose claims nothing runs. THE EXCEEDS ARM (kogaki#970), bound by a case and mutated once each, 2026-09-07, every mutation applied singly and restored. The rule: a member declaring `case_floor` with only a downward comparison FAILED, naming the member and the repair; the same member comparing in BOTH directions PASSED, which is the case that stops the deny passing vacuously by refusing everything; a member whose count identifier differs (the one JavaScript member spells it `CASE_COUNT`, not `N`) PASSED, the case that keeps the pattern keyed on the FLOOR's name so member N+1 is covered by the rule rather than by a list; a member declaring NO floor owed no arm; and a missing file was not double-reported here. The arms themselves were mutated against the live tree on `terrain-runtime`: a floor set BELOW the count (96 -> 95) failed on the upward arm naming the exact registry edit, a floor set ABOVE it (96 -> 97) failed on the downward arm with its kogaki#661 wording intact, and the unmutated floor passed — the control that the equality is an equality and not a check that refuses in every direction. Removing the upward arm from that member's file made THIS check red, which is the binding that closes the class: the repair cannot be quietly undone one member at a time. Recorded rather than asserted, on the convention this note already sets.

admission.contract: the consult-first discipline's reading act: reports the branch's consulted: receipt count and distinct pins, rendering zero explicitly — an obligation generates no event to hook, so observability is the whole remedy. Fails only on a malformed receipt, never on the count. Fenced-block quotations are MENTIONS of the grammar, not receipts, and are excluded from the counted set (kogaki#41, the PR #40 false positive). Parses the v2 continuation block (kogaki#28, story 1.10) — request_id, outcome, one query line per framing, indented under line one, all OPTIONAL so every v1 receipt in git history stays valid — and widens malformed to SIX field defects, all conformance rather than counting: an outcome outside the hub's ratified triple (a bare `miss` collapses the two causes the 2026-08-02 correction separated), a re-framed outcome recording fewer than every framing's query, an `uncovered-after-N` whose N disagrees with the number of query lines recorded (shape validation alone let a receipt claim seven framings while recording two), an N below the two-framing floor (a miss is not recordable as uncovered until re-asked along another axis; the floor is stated as its own clause because it is currently also implied by the query rule, and an implied invariant is one a refactor drops unnoticed), and a PARTIAL v2 receipt — continuations stay optional so a v1 receipt is valid, but once ANY continuation is present the receipt owes all three fields SPEC §4 requires (PR #43 review). The embedded fixture pass is the discrimination evidence, run every invocation, and asserts the PARSED FIELDS rather than only counts — a count-only assertion cannot observe whether the continuation fields were read at all, which measured 2 of 8 v2 cases discriminating before the assertion was widened and 6 of 8 after. States what it does NOT verify: the query-count rule is satisfied by two rephrasings of one question, and axis-variation is a judgment no count can observe — the check asserts the framings were RECORDED and routes whether they differed to the review lane, with a receipt found carrying two rephrasings as the observation that would earn a real detector. Empty values are handled by ONE rule applied in the parse: continuation PRESENCE is recorded as a fact about the text rather than inferred from value truthiness, and an empty value is absent for every field alike — before which empty query lines counted as recorded framings, so `uncovered-after-3-framings` with three blank queries satisfied N == len() (PR #43 re-review), and a `query:` line holding a SERIALIZED TOOL ARGUMENT rather than a question (kogaki#160 finding 4): the field is defined at the consultation map's Miss-postmortem field as the question verbatim, the grammar accepted any non-empty value, and `query: {"tag":"lessons/claude-code-ops"}` shipped on master passing every clause above — because the transport DERIVED the line, reading it off policy_lookup's own `question` argument and falling back to the raw --args JSON for every other tool, so a gloss_index consult had no field in which to record its question. gateway-query.mjs now requires `--question` per `--args` and refuses without it, making the emission unproducible on the tool path; this clause is the floor under condition 2's marked-exception path, and is the narrowest rule that discriminates — a value that is a JSON object/array end to end is a tool argument, while a question CONTAINING braces or quotes passes, with fixtures in both directions. Backward compatible by the scan window: this check reads merge-base..HEAD plus the PR body, never a file on the default branch and never the whole history, so receipts already merged lie outside every future scan and no branch fails on work it did not author. THE SECOND AXIS (kogaki#268): a `disposition:` continuation key carrying the GATE half — what the gate did with the consultation — on its own field rather than in `outcome:`, which is where the digest's vocabulary claim assumed it lived and where this check's own ratified-triple clause refuses it. Three vocabularies in this seam are called `outcome` and two of them are mutually exclusive in one slot, so the resolution is one field per axis, each owned by whoever must agree on it: the values are ADOPTED verbatim from the ratified closed two-value set (`auto-resolved-FYI | escalated`, spec-policy-fork-consultation §"Amended 2026-07-21 (triage, #519)", "no consumer-local extension") because a field read by both sides of the boundary is the boundary's and the boundary's owner is the hub (`topics/knowledge-architecture.md:31@dec0d568`), while the field's SHAPE is this repository's. The key is OPTIONAL and is deliberately NOT added to presence-implies-completeness' owed set: most consults here are not fork gates, and requiring the field would force a value on them. Recognising the key in the checker is a REQUIREMENT rather than a convenience — the continuation scan stops at the first unrecognised indented key, so a receipt carrying `disposition:` above its query lines parsed on the pre-#268 scanner as a field-less v1 line with every later field silently dropped, and 10 of the 12 new fixtures fail that scanner spliced against this fixture table. What it does NOT make substantiable, stated rather than implied: `consult-miss` and `degraded` stay uncountable from receipts under this or any schema — an unconsulted fork emits no receipt and a degraded consult emits none by design — so both are refused as values with that reason named, and the report line counts the two dispositions and says what nothing here can count WIDENED (kogaki#336): the grammar gains a THIRD continuation key, `axis:`, and it is the first that binds PER QUERY — upward to the nearest preceding `query:`, first declaration wins, an axis before any query orphaned and reported. The check validates SHAPE ONLY — position and a non-empty token — because the `subject | conduct` value set is the hub's to ratify under the boundary-field rule (product-lab@4cc496b topics/knowledge-architecture.md:50), so any value passes and unknown ones are reported and denied nowhere; the report NAMES the distinct axes rather than only counting them, which is what makes an unratified set observable while it is unratified. Eight per-query binding cases exercise both directions, plus an explicit never-gates assertion that an unknown axis is not reported malformed — the assertion standing between shape-only and this repository silently minting boundary values it does not own. Runtime re-measured 80 -> 95 ms (three local runs) for the widening rather than for an admission, because the binding quantity is cost per ship-cycle rather than member count.

admission.contract: the client kit's install guarantees, fired rather than merely written: fresh-install layout, idempotency, the one-line degrade at exit 11, the pinless-body deny, harness-loadable skill frontmatter, the entry-2 boundary (no kit tool reads gateway state), and the absence of any colocation default. Also the transport's RECEIPT MODE (kogaki#66, story 1.20), where the emitter replaces hand transcription: the refusal to assign the `outcome` token — `deferred-slot: consult-outcome-token-assignment` is FILLED (owner decision 2026-08-06, kogaki#66 — the OPERATOR supplies the token), so a default would reinstate the guess the fill declined and the refusal must still name the slot rather than read as a syntax error; that a degraded run emits NO receipt block, because a receipt for a consult that did not happen is the fabrication the clause exists to prevent; that receipt mode is opt-in, so the pre-1.20 invocation is byte-for-byte unchanged; that the marked-exception key is the fixed UNINDENTED `consult-receipt:` token, which is correctness rather than style because check-consult-receipts.sh recognises only request_id/outcome/query as continuation keys and an unrecognised indented key above them ends the continuation scan, leaving a field-less v1 line that silently passes; and the emitter's own 13-case composition fixture pass, which asserts line one is COPIED from the served response rather than re-derived, one query line per framing actually run, pins merged under one commit, the token carried untouched, and five refusals where the wire did not carry what a receipt asserts. Also the consult ENTRY POINT (kogaki#94, story 1.21), whose properties are all properties of the INVOCATION rather than of the wire and so are decidable without a reachable gateway: that there is exactly ONE receipt composer and the entry point is not a second one, routing through the transport instead; that a verdict-shaped input is corrected AT THE POINT OF USE and never forwarded (exit 3), and that the correction is an affordance — `--restate` re-submits the corrected claim in the same act and the run then reaches the wire, which is the only observable distinguishing an affordance from a nicer denial; that `--outcome` is required at the entry point as on the transport, with the refusal naming the OPERATOR, because the entry point is the surface a session touches; that the two-framings floor is carried at the call in BOTH directions (refused with what the re-framing owes, and proceeding once the second framing is supplied), since a floor that refused everything would pass a one-directional test; that the framing COUNT is emitted as the transport fact it is and a token contradicting it is refused rather than repaired, repair being the tool assigning the token by the back door; that the re-framing bound is ONE, never a search loop; and that the exit-11 degraded path is STATED with its example receipt marker UNINDENTED above line one, asserted on the emitted text because a wrong example is a wrong receipt in every PR that follows it. What no case on either surface covers is a LIVE consult, which the test states rather than leaves to look covered. Registered because a test nothing invokes is the orphan-guard shape kogaki#6 was filed to end Also the ISSUE-CHECKPOINT CONTENT-LIVENESS half (kogaki#188), where the guarantee is that a pass-claim matches what was actually compared: that the THIRD entry point `--emit-pin-quotes` owes the same one-line exit-11 degrade as the other two, because it is the WRITER for the stored quote hash and a writer that emits a short list on an unreachable seam reads as a complete one; and the tool's own content-liveness fixture pass, which is pure and gateway-free and asserts the whitespace-normalized hash (a reflowed served line is the same quote, while a case flip is not), use-vs-mention on BOTH the pin-quote and consulted grammars, a DECLARED served-address map that returns cannot-tell rather than guessing an address, the live topics/articles.md:79 drift blocked AND located at :80 as the regression pin (the dangerous form is the pin that still RESOLVES, so a resolution check cannot catch it), three results rather than two with `verified` reachable only through a fetch that returned records in scope, and an output that never implies liveness it did not check. Widened at this admission act rather than left to be inferred from the case list Also the SHAPE READ and the EMISSION DUTY (kogaki#325/#326, stories 1.48/1.49), the kit's two default-on consumer clauses, whose install-time properties are decidable without a reachable gateway and are therefore asserted here: that the shape read is gitignored EXACTLY ONCE across two installs and that the emission directory is NOT gitignored — the two assertions are deliberately INVERSE, because the artifacts answer the same axis oppositely on source sensitivity rather than on file kind, and asserting only one would leave a later change free to 'make them consistent' and destroy the distinction the spec exists to record, with the failure silent and, on a public repository, irreversible once pushed; that the managed CLAUDE.md block carries BOTH clauses, since specs/spec-client-kit/SPEC.md §2 refuses skill-as-sole-carrier and a clause reaching only the sittings that invoke a skill is the failure the default carrier exists to prevent; that the shape read degrades in ONE line at exit 11 like every other kit tool, which the install itself depends on because a hard failure there would break the ratified degraded-install-is-a-valid-install promise for every consumer; that the emission writer produces the five fixed fields at a dated, slugged path, prints that path as an in-session receipt, and refuses an undeclared grain, the set being closed like every other declaration here; that the emitted text ITSELF states it is a candidate and not a promotion, asserted on the artifact rather than trusted to the prose above it, because §4.2's emission-is-not-promotion boundary is this writer's entire standing; that the plain-register note REPORTS without refusing and the write still exits 0, a channel that rejects your words being a channel you stop using; and both tools' own gateway-free fixture passes. What no case here covers is a LIVE digest composition, which needs a reachable seam and is stated rather than left to look covered. Also the OWNER REGISTER's install-time half (kogaki#320, story 1.50): that the owner-render fixture pass runs; that the RELAY RULE in the installed skill points at the kit's emission and assigns the Conclusion to the agent — asserted against the INSTALLED copy, which is what caught this story editing the installed file while leaving the kit SOURCE untouched, the kogaki#285 divergence reproduced live and fixed in the same act; and that a DEGRADED consult emits NEITHER register, because a rendering of an answer that was never served is the same fabrication the no-receipt-on-degrade rule already forbids. Separability (AC2) is asserted where transportArgv lives rather than here — the entry point is not import-safe, so a node -e import cannot reach the function; this member invokes that pass and the arrangement is named in the test so the coverage stays findable. Also the DELTA STEP (kogaki#334, story 1.51), which is the shape read's §3.4 act and the first case here that needs a STUB GATEWAY: the earlier shape-read cases establish properties of a RENDERING, decidable from a degrade and a pure fixture pass, whereas a delta is a property of a COMPARISON against a live regeneration — a vendored pin differing from a served one — and no state of an unreachable gateway produces that, so the wire is doubled rather than the content asserted. Four properties, all on emitted text: that a stale vendored pin REPORTS AND EXITS 0, because §3.5's enhancer-never-dependency property makes a pre-step that gates a sitting the defect rather than the feature; that no vendored digest AT ALL is its own third state and also exits 0, an absent digest and an unchanged one being the same quiet and different facts; that the output is PIN-FREE — no `consulted:`, no `request_id:`, no `@<sha>` — because §8 puts pins on the machine-facing side and a delta shown before a sitting is the one shape-read output an owner reads directly, asserted on live text as well as in the fixture pass since the fixture composes its own inputs while this carries a real pin through the whole composer; and that `--delta` owes the same one-line exit-11 degrade every other kit tool owes. Also the PER-TERM DENOMINATOR (§3.1's clause as amended by kogaki#334), which is the element-level three-state rendering PR #335 landed, surviving one grain down: `if (e.soft) continue;` made a term whose own `glossary_entry` read could not be parsed indistinguishable from one carrying no state line, so the section rendered its survivors as the whole in-scope set. The stub serves an unparseable body for one in-scope term and the case asserts that term is COUNTED AND NAMED in the digest — an end-to-end assertion the gateway-free fixtures cannot make, and the reason this widening is not simply more fixture cases. AND, added kogaki#285, the BYTE-EQUALITY of the kit source `policy/kit/skills/consult-first.md` with THIS repository's installed copy `.claude/skills/consult-first/SKILL.md` — asserted over the real tree rather than the temp install, because `install.sh` copies source over copy and a divergence is a pending SILENT DELETION of whichever side is not the source rather than a conflict. The kit's own test structurally cannot carry this: it installs into `mktemp -d` and asserts over a result that is a `cp` of the source by construction, so it passes identically while the committed copy has drifted. THE CLAUDE CLI IS A TEST DOUBLE (kogaki#787). `install.sh` step 5 shells out to `claude mcp list` on every run and `claude mcp add` when a gateway is configured; the test now prepends a shim directory to PATH whose `claude` records its argv and answers `mcp list` from a per-scenario body. THE RULE. The Harness owns the Terrain workflow and executes its Acts, and ownership is determined by which component executes each Act rather than by where an instruction is written. A skill file addressed to the session -- how to invoke the executor, what to render, what to compose, what never to do -- hands those Acts back to the model whatever the surrounding prose claims. The file is therefore reduced to what the harness needs to find it plus the one line that starts the run, and this member holds it there.

THE NAMED DEFECT, measured rather than feared. Across kogaki#17 through #890 (2026-08-05 to 2026-09-05) the workflow was specified as Harness-controlled and every implementation satisfied the words while leaving every Act that mattered to the model. The skill file was 158 lines of conduct at the head this member was admitted on. Across every retained session transcript the tag question was passed to the question UI ZERO times, and on 2026-09-09 two runs showed no table and no question at all. Prose telling the model to do the right thing had been the whole mechanism, and it had been failing silently for a month. The position this rests on, quoted at its pin: "A rule is enforced only at the layer where it can be broken -- a prohibition needs a mechanical gate at the tool boundary because prose is advisory to a system whose job is to satisfy instructions." (consulted: product-lab@4a58f2a3a895ffa358115db2ad38cb95a56b5523 LESSONS.md:209)

THE PREDICATE IS OVER THE FILE'S SHAPE, NEVER OVER ITS MEANING, and that is what makes the member admissible where a conduct-detector would not be. It reads no line's content and judges no sentence: it partitions the file by position at the frontmatter fence and asserts the region after it is exactly one line beginning `!`. A file that grows a sentence fails whatever the sentence says. That is the point -- the defect class is "conduct came back", and conduct has no closed vocabulary, so a matcher over English would yield candidates a reader must judge and would pass the first paragraph phrased around its term list.

admission.contract:
Every row of every `src/` THE NAMES THIS FILE USES table names something its own file names. The predicate is the INVERSE of the usual staleness check and that direction is the whole design: "does every reference have a row?" cannot see a surplus row, and only "does every row name a source?" can (consulted: product-lab@aecb3b52ea46b357a7e7c39b81b1a26c0deeff0e LESSONS.md:191).

THE NAMED DEFECT. PR #984 wrote 24 such tables from a read of `governing`/`governing_text` alone — an input narrower than the files' own reference surface. The tables it produced named a name no file uses (`src/deps-registry.json`'s "The enumeration and its non-member fallback", raised at round 1 of that PR and untouched by the fix) and dropped two names two files do use. The narrowing was introduced WHILE repairing a narrowing, at round 2 of 2, with no round left to catch it.

THE DECLINED DIRECTION, stated at birth so the coverage is not read as total: "every name the file uses has a row" is not mechanically decidable here, because a reference is written in free prose (`[see: SPEC-x "Name"]`, `(SPEC-x, the name; kogaki#N)`, `SPEC-x §"Name"`) and a matcher over it yields candidates a reader must judge, not failures. That direction was discharged BY HAND for kogaki#987 over every line of all 25 carriers and its record is in that PR; this member holds the half that is a tree fact.

DECLARED LIMITS, in the check's own words beside the predicate: it does not verify that a row's spec label is the right spec, that the spec section still exists, or that a name the file uses is missing a row. The first two are reads against another repository's text and the third is the undecidable direction; all three stay with review. A file carrying the pointer block and no table (`src/render-figure.mjs`, which states at the site that no string in it names a spec at all) satisfies the predicate vacuously and its zero is printed rather than passing silently.

No file under `src/` names a spec SECTION NUMBER. `src/SPEC-REFERENCES.md`'s "What a reference never names" states the rule on measured ground -- a number renumbers, and the line range `src/cite-check.mjs` used to print had already drifted onto an unrelated bullet while three of `src/runs.mjs`'s section numbers did not resolve to the content they were cited for. Both were found by two review rounds reading ONE diff (PR #989 rounds 1 and 2), the second only after the first was reported and answered; neither was found by any act that runs on every head. The rule was carried by reading alone.

THE PREDICATE IS OVER THE FORBIDDEN FORM, NEVER OVER REFERENCES, and that is what makes this member admissible where `check-names-tables.sh` declined its forward direction at birth. That decline's ground is that a REFERENCE is written in free prose, so a matcher over it yields candidates a reader must judge. This check matches no reference: it matches a section sign, optional whitespace, a digit -- a closed form with no grammar to parse. A hit is a failure, never a candidate. The sibling's ground therefore does not transfer, and is not inherited by analogy.

NO EXEMPTION LIST, chosen rather than inherited. Two `src/` sites hold this pattern as REGEX SOURCE (`src/assemble.mjs`'s leak-guard constant, which runs the same predicate in production for the owner-facing half of this rule, and `src/draft.mjs`'s self-test); neither matches, because in regex source the section sign is followed by a backslash. `src/assemble.mjs`'s comment naming its own specimen writes it escaped and says so at the site. So the convention keeping the tree clean is textual and already established, and this member adds no blessed-path list a later site could be quietly added to.

THE POPULATION IS MEASURED, not residual (kogaki#991 acceptance 2). The sweep ran at kogaki@3cf7cb0, the head BEFORE the fix: 8 `§` sites across 32 `src/` files, of which exactly 2 were the defect. The other 6 are the rule's own grammar specimen, the two regex literals above, the licensed `§"name"` form, and two issue-section names carrying no number. The 8 is pinned to that head deliberately: the carrier that STATES the count is itself a `src/` file writing about the form, so it adds licensed and escaped `§` sites of its own and any later head sweeps to a LARGER number. The figure that does not move is the defect count, 2, which this member holds at zero from that head onward.

DECLARED LIMITS, in the check's own words beside the predicate: it does not verify that a reference names the right spec, that a named section still exists, that a quoted heading is accurate, or that a LINE RANGE is absent -- the rule's other half. The first three are reads against another repository's text and stay with review. The fourth is declined at birth: a line range is bare digits indistinguishable from every other number in these files, so a matcher for it would be the candidate-generator this member exists by not being.

`src/workflow.json`'s `entry_point_accounting` states an invariant over the runtime: EVERY case in `src/terrain.mjs`'s dispatcher appears in exactly one of the five maps beside it (`bound_to_a_state`, `removed_entry_points`, `retired_entry_points`, `non_flow_entry_points`, `owner_executed_entry_points`), and a case in none of them, or in two, is by that file's own sentence a defect against it. This member computes it. No other registered member reaches the contract: `terrain-runtime` runs the Terrain runtime's fixture pass and never reads these maps.

THE NAMED DEFECT. Nothing computed the totality. A `git grep` over all five map names at kogaki#986 found no reader anywhere in the repository -- only the declaration itself and one policy emission discussing it. At the head before kogaki#901 the invariant DID NOT HOLD: `run` was a dispatcher case in none of the five maps. It stood through at least the #856 and #861 sittings, both of which edited these very maps, and was found only because a pickup computed the totality by hand while reading for something else. #901 repaired the gap; it did not give the invariant a reader, so the tree could violate the sentence again indefinitely and nothing would go red.

THE TEXT GUARD IS KEPT BESIDE THE INSTRUMENT, never replaced by it. Arm (d) asserts that `entry_point_accounting` still STATES the totality and that it NAMES this file, so the declaration and its reader retire together or not at all, and an editor of these maps learns from the declaration itself that a reader exists -- kogaki#986 acceptance 3. A reader nothing points at is one the next editor works around.

A MEMBER OF ITS OWN RATHER THAN A FOLD-IN, which kogaki#986 left as an open fork (its own registered check, or an assertion inside `src/terrain.mjs self-test`). The fold-in arm's only argument is that a further member is itself a cost, and the served kernel strikes it: the binding quantity is total cost per ship-cycle rather than member count. And `check-terrain-runtime.sh`'s own record already declined a fold-in for the reason that reaches this contract unchanged -- it would put two contracts behind one removal signal, and this contract's removal signal (the declaration's sentence leaving the tree) has nothing to do with the Terrain runtime's fixtures.

THE ENUMERATION BOUND IS STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED, which kogaki#986 asks for by name. A regex over `case "...":`, SCOPED to the span from `switch (cmd) {` to the first `default:`; no language-aware parser, which would be a dependency and a second thing to be wrong. Five declared limits sit beside the predicate in the file: it reads TEXT, so a `case` inside a string or comment in the span reads as a case, and the span is not short -- it runs to the FIRST `default:` and so swallows the ~1,100-line `self-test` case body, which is where fixture strings shaped like case labels would grow (L1); it assumes ONE dispatcher, asserted by arm (c) rather than believed (L2); `default:` is the span's terminator and so is excluded by construction rather than by a filter someone could drop (L3); the REVERSE direction is never asserted, because `removed_entry_points` and `retired_entry_points` hold entry points that are deliberately not cases any more, so `every map key is a case` is false by design for two of the five (L4); and it does not judge WHICH map is right, which is a judgment about meaning and would be a lint over judgment (L5).

ARM (b) MUTATES A SYNTHESISED BASELINE, NEVER THE LIVE DECLARATION, and that is its soundness rather than a convenience. Mutating the tree's own accounting makes every mutant inherit whatever is already wrong with it: measured during this admission on a tree where `run` was already in no map, the drop-mutant changed nothing, the plant-mutant yielded exactly one, and the control arm re-reported (a)'s real defect as `the reader misfires`. The discrimination arm went silent and then actively lied in precisely the state it exists to be trusted in. The baseline is now well-formed by construction over the LIVE dispatcher's case names, so (b) says the same thing about the instrument whether (a) passes or fails, and the specimen is still the real one.

admission.contract: THE JUDGMENT STATES ARE THE EXECUTOR'S OWN MODEL CALLS, AND THE SPAN THEY SIT IN COMPLETES IN ONE HOOK EVENT (kogaki#1030). What no other member reaches is that this is a property of a WHOLE SPAN rather than of any function: `src/terrain.mjs self-test` drives composers and readers over inputs it constructs, so it can assert what a judgment state REFUSES and never that a run gets through one. FOUR CONTRACTS. (1) ACCEPTANCE 1: one synthesized PostToolUse payload for the tag answer carries `compose_input`, `J1_claims`, `J2_subdivision` and the `cotag_groups` write in a SINGLE invocation, ending awaiting `ID_SELECTION` with its declaration written -- so `reports/CoTagGroups.md` exists before the ID question is offered, which is the guarantee kogaki#1030 was filed to obtain -- and EVERY transition of that span is attributed to that payload's `tool_use_id`, because a span is what one hook event executed and the record must say so. (2) ACCEPTANCE 2: a judge stub returning a record the state's OWN refusals reject fails the run after the attempts the table's `retries` licenses, carrying the state's refusal text verbatim, and writes no display. (3) ACCEPTANCE 3: one payload for the ID answer reaches `reports/FullReport.md` and the `STRAND_SELECTION` declaration. (4) ACCEPTANCE 4, the REMOVAL TEST: all three hold in a tree carrying the runtime and the hooks with `specs/` absent and the skill file reduced to its one `!` line -- a claim about the TREE, which no pass running inside the full tree can make. THE JUDGE AND THE SEAM ARE BOTH STUBBED, and by different instruments for the same reason: the judge through `KOGAKI_JUDGE_CLI`, which replaces the BINARY and leaves the argv, the parse, the retry bound and every refusal the shipped ones; the gateway by a scratch REPO carrying a stub `policy/kit/bin/gateway-query.mjs`, which is `terrain-runtime`'s own recipe. So these cases exercise shipped code rather than a second path written for them. NOT ASSERTED, stated rather than left to look covered: that the pinned model is REACHABLE or that its answers are good. The stub stands in for the model, so this member binds the executor's call, parse, retry and refusal and never the judgment -- which is not this repository's to assert, on `gate-capture-hook`'s own ground about facts belonging to a machine rather than to a repository. TWO MORE CONTRACTS ADDED AT PR #1044 ROUND 1, each binding a repair that round asked for. (5) THE RETRY WINDOW IS AS WIDE AS THE LICENCE: a judge response that is not JSON is re-asked to the same bound and the run then fails naming the parse refusal -- before the repair the window wrapped only the conformance check, so an unparseable response exited on the FIRST call while `retries` bounded one arm of three. (6) THE PER-CALL BOUND IS DECLARED IN THE TABLE: `judge.timeout_s` is present and positive. That one is asserted as a CARRIER rather than by driving a slow judge, and the reason is stated rather than left: a case that waited out a real timeout would add its own bound to the suite's runtime in order to prove that a bound exists. (7) THE PERSISTED RUN RECORD NAMES THE REFUSAL, not only stderr: the record carries `judgment_refusals.<state>` with the verbatim refusal and the number of attempts made. Acceptance 2 says the RECORD names it, and stderr and the record are different carriers -- the second is the one still there when a reader comes back to the run, which is the only time anyone reads a failed run at all. CONTRACT (8), ADDED AT kogaki#1068: THE SubGroup RULES BIND INSIDE THE RE-ASK WINDOW, AND THE ASK STATES THEM. The per-label member caps, `min_subgroup_members`, the residual bound and the placement cover were enforced in `subgroupPlacement` and `judgeSubgroup`, which only the two RENDER states call; `J2_subdivision` -- the state holding the bounded per-group re-ask -- validated the ENVELOPE alone (`judged: true`, `subgroups` an array). So a record breaching a rule passed J2, spent every group's call, and failed the run at `cotag_groups` with a refusal the judge never saw. Three cases: a stub whose first answer for one group puts every member in one `tight` SubGroup and whose second splits them advances the run with exactly ONE refusal against that group, whose text names the cap AND the `report-format.json` key it was read from; a stub that leaves one member unplaced on every call fails the state after the table's declared bound naming the group and the member, and writes NO assembled `terrain-judge-J2_subdivision.json`; and the per-group ask's own input carries a `limits` block whose numbers EQUAL `report-format.json`'s, compared against the file rather than against a literal. THEY NEED A THIRD TREE, and that is the contract's own precondition rather than a convenience: every other tree in this member composes co-tag groups of TWO members, under which the `tight` cap of 5 can never fire and no member can be left over -- so no fixture here could construct the defect at all. The wide tree serves one group of six beside one of two, through an environment override on the SAME gateway stub rather than a second one, because a second served surface is free to drift from the first. CONTRACT (9), ADDED AT PR #1070 ROUND 1: THE TWO CARRIER PROPERTIES (8)'s OWN DECLARATIONS CLAIM. Both are asserted STRUCTURALLY over the source and the table rather than by driving a run, and each has its own reason. (a) Every judgment state declaring `limits` names a block `JUDGE_LIMIT_BLOCKS` carries, AND `invokeJudge` resolves the key BEFORE the `per_group` branch. Resolved inside the branch -- which is how (8) first shipped -- a state declaring the key without `per_group` got no limits block in its ask and never reached the unknown-block-name refusal, both silently: exactly the two properties the `field_semantics` row claims, false. There is no such state in the shipped table, so there is nothing to drive, and a fixture that added one would be asserting a table nobody ships. (b) `SUBGROUP_MEMBERS_DO_NOT_SUM` is raised at exactly ONE site, and that site is inside `subgroupPlacement`. It lived at the co-tag display alone -- so the report's two placement sites never carried it -- and (8) arrived with a second copy beside it, two wordings citing two different grounds on their first day. How many places one refusal is written is a property of the source and of no run. The member also asserts its own subject is present and exited 0 before reading any decision, because a missing or crashed hook is otherwise indistinguishable from one that deliberately admitted.
